intent: To demonstrate that income inequality, measured by the ratio of household income at the 90th percentile to the 10th percentile, has increased steadily since 1980.

requirements.question: Must the video convey an overall upward trend from 1980 to 2019?
Must the clip show monotonic/steady increase across all consecutive benchmark years, not just an overall endpoint rise?

units.claim: The relative income-inequality measure is higher in 2019 than in 1980, showing an overall upward trend.
accept: The inequality indicator rises overall from 1980 to 2019.
The series ends higher than it starts.
There is a net upward movement from the first to the last benchmark year.
units.evidence: Both the 1980 and 2019 relative-value marks must be visible, and the 2019 mark must be higher than the 1980 mark.

units.claim: The rise is steady: each successive benchmark year has a higher relative_value than the previous year (1980 < 1990 < 2000 < 2010 < 2019).
accept: The indicator increases at every benchmark step.
No benchmark year is lower than the one before it.
The series is monotonically rising across the listed years.
units.evidence: Consecutive benchmark-year relative-value marks must appear in increasing order, with no downward step between them.

optional_valid: The clip may name the metric as the 90th/10th household income ratio, provided it uses only relative comparisons and no absolute income values.
The clip may note that the five years are benchmark observations rather than annual data.
The clip may display intermediate benchmark values 1990=0.4788, 2000=0.5024, and 2010=0.5546.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
